newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa eases capital controls in budget.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa eases capital controls in budget.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced the next steps in the easing of exchange controls in his maiden budget on Wednesday, giving individuals the right to invest some funds directly overseas.
Manuel told parliament that private individuals would be able to invest a limited amount directly outside the country or alternatively hold foreign currency deposits with South African banks.
The move will take effect from July 1 and an announcement regarding specific amounts will be made in due course.
Companies are also being given increased freedom to invest overseas as part of a move which Manuel said represented a change in philosophy on capital controls.

"We move now to an environment in which South Africans can make ordinary transactions abroad freely, while the constraints which remain on large movements of capital will increasingly give way to procedural and prudential supervision," he said.

Elsewhere, Manuel's keenly-awaited budget focused on a cut in real spending to deliver a promised deficit before borrowing of 4.0 percent of gross domestic product in the year to March 31, 1998, against 5.1 percent in 1996/97.
Cutting the deficit is a central plank of the government's macroeconomic strategy, announced last year, which is designed to double economic growth to six percent a year by the end of the century.
